messages:
alex: Quick sync — putting a draft routing decision framework on the table. Goal: give product + sales a small set of deterministic routing outcomes (latency-first, cost-first, residency-isolated) we can commit to for Q3 launches.

marta: +1. Can you sketch the minimal policy matrix? Customers keep asking for explicit guarantees. :eyes:

alex: Rough sketch: 
- Policy A: global-low-latency (route to nearest healthy region, fallback to compatible model variants)
- Policy B: cost-conservative (batching and spot-capacity first, higher queueing tolerance)
- Policy C: jurisdictional-isolated (traffic pinned to allowed regions, no fallback outside allowed set)

kevin: Need to be explicit about migration. If we enforce Policy C, what happens when a region is degraded? Silent failures for customers is unacceptable.

alex: Agreed. For Policy C we propose: 
1) Hard pin by default, 
2) Canary alerting to customer and automatic read-only fallback to a cached embeddings path if region unavailable, 
3) Ops-runbook triggers for migration.

rynnah: That read-only fallback is interesting — would it be a documented SLA deviation? customers will want that spelled out in contracts.

marta: Also: telemetry. We need token-level visibility (latency + cost delta) when policy changes are applied. If we roll out cost-conservative for a tenant, we must show expected token cost reduction and P50/P99 latency delta.

kevin: On the infra side, two constraints: model variant compatibility matrix (quantized vs fp16) and KV-cache consistency across regions. If we route across variants, we must guarantee prompt-prefix equivalence or annotate outputs as degraded.

alex: Proposal for rollout criteria: 
- Beta: internal + 2 pilot customers, must pass canary for 48h with no >2% error rate impact and <10% P99 latency regression for latency-first.
- GA: 30 customer-days of healthy telemetry, two independent region failover tests, signed-off runbook.

marta: customer asks to prioritize Policy C for regulated customers. That bumps the migration/ops work — recommend we schedule Policy C for Dedicated/private channels first, then hosted.

kevin: Technical debt note: we need a small policy-DSL to encode rules. Example YAML (very rough):
```yaml
policy: jurisdictional-isolated
allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
fallback: cached_embeddings
fallback_ttl: 24h
notify: ops@redwood
```

rynnah: I like the DSL. Add `model_variant_whitelist` and `sla_tier` fields so sales can map offers to policies.

infra-bot: CI: linked PR #4223 (routing/dsl) queued. Auto-tests: policy-parser, region-sim, fallback-playbook.

alex: Next steps I propose: 
- kaizen doc draft (owner: me) with decision matrix + launch criteria by EOD Friday
- kevin to prototype policy-parser spike (1 week)
- marta to surface top 3 customers to pilot Policy C and get NDA/contacts

marta: I'll kick off outreach. Also, include a small pricing delta for cost-conservative and jurisdictional-isolated lanes — PM will need that for CAC modelling.

kevin: I'll land a prototype branch and attach perf microbenchmarks. Will call out quantization compatibility.

rynnah: Ops: I'll draft playbooks for: region failover, data residency audit, and customer-facing behavior docs (what we promise).

alex: Thanks — tagging follow-ups: @marta @kevin @rynnah. If no objections, I'll post the first draft doc to the infra design repo and schedule a 30m sync next Tue. :thumbsup:

kevin: :+1:

marta: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Reminder: design doc template located at https://git.internal/redwood/docs/designs/routing-policy-template.md
